Exact finite checks q=2 n=4,5 and q=3 n=4 corroborate the equations but are not used as infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Sanchez arXiv:1108.0451 gives general finite p-negative-type determinant methods and complete bipartite examples; Murugan arXiv:1112.5657 gives a general vertex-transitive determinant criterion and Hamming cube examples. Neither inspected text includes the q-Grassmann rank-two graph invariant or the heat-kernel phase classification. Harandi et al. arXiv:1407.1123 analyze kernels on real continuous Grassmannians, not finite fields. Related published finite Grassmannian Fourier projection findings concern different operators. Residual risk: combinations of classical Grassmann graph spectra and general negative-type theory could supply an unindexed equivalent result; no categorical uniqueness is claimed.
residual_risks: A past non-indexed treatment may already substitute known q-Grassmann adjacency eigenvalues into Murugan/Sánchez negative-type criteria, yielding the same sharp p*.

The q-Grassmann p=1 kernel eigenvalues may be well known as a routine special case of a classical association-scheme transform; searches did not conclusively rule out an equivalent whole phase diagram.
Indexed sources and accessible full texts do not constitute exhaustive global proof of novelty.

value.rationale: The generalized-roundness endpoint of a natural infinite family, the exact minimal Euclidean snowflake embedding dimension and its discontinuous drop, and the all-parameter positive-definiteness region of a canonical powered graph-distance heat kernel are mathematically motivated exact invariants. In particular the natural p=1 kernel has sharp strength threshold a=log q independent of n and a rank-[n]_q boundary. This is more than a renamed known criterion or arbitrary finite experiment.
